task1.title: Two road tunnels in two Australian cities
task1.prompt: The diagrams below give information about two road tunnels in two Australian cities.

stages.label: Tunnel A
stages.detail: Built between 1987–1992 for $556 million; spans 2.2 kilometres in length at a depth of 25 metres beneath water/bridge; twin tube cross-section with 2 lanes per tube.

stages.label: Tunnel B
stages.detail: Built between 2004–2007 for $1.1 billion; spans 3.6 kilometres in length at a depth of 35 metres beneath a city surface; twin tube cross-section with 3 lanes per tube.

chartDesc.overview: The diagram compares two twin-tube Australian road tunnels, detailing their construction years, cost, depth, length, surrounding environment, and lane capacity.
keyFeatures: Tunnel A passes under water beneath a suspension bridge, whereas Tunnel B passes directly beneath a city/ground surface road.
Tunnel B is longer (3.6 km vs 2.2 km), deeper (35 m vs 25 m), more expensive ($1.1 billion vs $556 million), and wider (3 lanes per tube vs 2 lanes per tube) than Tunnel A.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.
task1.sampleBand8:
The two diagrams compare a pair of road tunnels built beneath waterways in different Australian cities, showing when each was built, what it cost, and its dimensions and cross-section.

Overall, Tunnel B is the larger, deeper, longer and much more expensive of the two, and was completed more than a decade after Tunnel A. Both, however, share the same basic twin-tube design, in which two separate tubes carry traffic in opposite directions.

Tunnel A was constructed between 1987 and 1992 at a cost of 556 million dollars. It runs 2.2 kilometres beneath a harbour that is spanned by a suspension bridge, at a depth of 25 metres. Its cross-section reveals two tubes, each wide enough to accommodate two lanes of vehicles side by side.

Tunnel B, built much later between 2004 and 2007, was far costlier, at 1.1 billion dollars — roughly double the price of Tunnel A. It is also considerably bigger in every respect: it stretches 3.6 kilometres, lies 35 metres below the surface, and passes under a road rather than a river. Although it uses the same twin-tube configuration, each of its tubes is wider, holding three lanes of traffic instead of two, which helps to explain its substantially higher cost.

Ikkita diagramma turli Avstraliya shaharlarida suv yo'llari ostida qurilgan bir juft avtomobil tunnelini solishtirib, har biri qachon qurilgani, qancha turgani hamda uning o'lchamlari va ko'ndalang kesimini ko'rsatadi.

Umuman olganda, B tunnel ikkalasining kattarog'i, chuqurrog'i, uzunrog'i va ancha qimmatrog'i bo'lib, A tunneldan o'n yildan ko'proq vaqt keyin yakunlangan. Biroq ikkalasi ham bir xil asosiy ikki quvurli dizaynga ega bo'lib, unda ikkita alohida quvur transportni qarama-qarshi yo'nalishlarda o'tkazadi.

A tunnel 1987–1992-yillar oralig'ida 556 million dollar sarflab qurilgan. U osma ko'prik bilan bog'langan buxta ostida 25 metr chuqurlikda 2,2 kilometrga cho'ziladi. Uning ko'ndalang kesimi ikkita quvurni ko'rsatadi, ularning har biri ikkita qator transportni yonma-yon joylashtirishga yetarlicha keng.

Ancha keyin, 2004–2007-yillarda qurilgan B tunnel esa 1,1 milliard dollar bilan ancha qimmatga tushgan — bu A tunnel narxidan qariyb ikki baravar ko'p. U barcha jihatdan ham sezilarli darajada kattaroq: 3,6 kilometrga cho'ziladi, sirtdan 35 metr pastda joylashgan va daryo emas, balki yo'l ostidan o'tadi. Garchi u xuddi shu ikki quvurli tuzilishdan foydalansa-da, uning har bir quvuri kengroq bo'lib, ikkita emas, uchta qator transportni sig'diradi — bu uning sezilarli darajada yuqori narxini izohlashga yordam beradi.

task2.title: Private companies funding scientific research
task2.prompt: In today's world, private companies, rather than the government, pay for and conduct most scientific research. Do you think the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
task2.sampleBand8:
In the modern world an ever-growing share of scientific research is funded and carried out by private corporations rather than by governments. In my view, although this trend brings real dangers, its advantages ultimately outweigh them, provided the state maintains a supervisory role.

There are strong arguments in its favour. Private firms possess vast resources and can invest far more, and far faster, than cash-strapped governments; the pharmaceutical and technology industries, for example, pour billions into research every year. Because their survival depends on results, companies also tend to work efficiently and to turn discoveries into practical products quickly, which speeds up innovation and benefits consumers. Crucially, this relieves the taxpayer of an enormous financial burden, freeing public money for schools, hospitals and other pressing needs.

The disadvantages, however, are genuine. Businesses naturally prioritise research that is profitable, so unglamorous but vital fields — rare diseases, basic physics, climate science — may be neglected because they promise little return. There is also a risk that findings will be suppressed or distorted when they threaten a company's interests, and that expensive results will be locked behind patents instead of shared for the public good. These are serious concerns, but they argue for regulation rather than for rejecting private funding altogether.

In conclusion, I believe the benefits of private research — greater investment, efficiency and relief for public finances — outweigh its drawbacks. The wisest approach is a partnership in which private money drives most research while governments fund neglected areas and regulate the rest to protect the public interest.
task2.uzSampleBand8:
Zamonaviy dunyoda ilmiy tadqiqotlarning tobora ortib borayotgan ulushi hukumatlar emas, balki xususiy korporatsiyalar tomonidan moliyalashtiriladi va olib boriladi. Menimcha, bu tendensiya chinakam xatarlar keltirsa-da, agar davlat nazorat rolini saqlab qolsa, uning afzalliklari pirovardida ulardan ustun keladi.

Uning foydasiga kuchli dalillar bor. Xususiy firmalar ulkan resurslarga ega bo'lib, mablag' tanqisligini boshdan kechirayotgan hukumatlardan ancha ko'proq va ancha tezroq sarmoya kirita oladi; masalan, farmatsevtika va texnologiya sohalari har yili tadqiqotga milliardlab dollar quyadi. Omon qolishi natijalarga bog'liq bo'lgani uchun kompaniyalar samarali ishlashga va kashfiyotlarni tezda amaliy mahsulotga aylantirishga moyil bo'ladi, bu esa innovatsiyani tezlashtiradi va iste'molchilarga foyda keltiradi. Eng muhimi, bu soliq to'lovchini ulkan moliyaviy yukdan xalos qiladi va davlat mablag'ini maktablar, kasalxonalar va boshqa dolzarb ehtiyojlar uchun bo'shatadi.

Biroq kamchiliklari ham haqiqiy. Bizneslar tabiiy ravishda foydali tadqiqotlarni ustuvor biladi, shu bois jozibasiz, ammo hayotiy muhim sohalar — kam uchraydigan kasalliklar, fundamental fizika, iqlim fani — kam daromad va'da qilgani uchun e'tibordan chetda qolishi mumkin. Natijalar kompaniya manfaatlariga tahdid solganda bostirilishi yoki buzib ko'rsatilishi, qimmat natijalar esa jamiyat manfaati uchun bo'lishilmasdan patentlar ortiga qulflanib qolishi xavfi ham bor. Bular jiddiy tashvishlar, ammo ular xususiy moliyalashtirishni butunlay rad etishni emas, tartibga solishni talab qiladi.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, men xususiy tadqiqotning foydalari — ko'proq sarmoya, samaradorlik va davlat moliyasi uchun yengillik — uning kamchiliklaridan ustun keladi deb hisoblayman. Eng oqilona yondashuv — xususiy mablag' tadqiqotlarning ko'pini ilgari suradigan, hukumatlar esa e'tibordan chetdagi sohalarni moliyalashtirib, qolganini jamoat manfaatini himoya qilish uchun tartibga soladigan hamkorlikdir.
